text:
**Short version:** choose **Monzo** if you mostly bank by app and value spending tools and travel convenience. Choose **Nationwide** if having branches and in-person help matters, or you want access to its wider range of current-account options. Both are fee-free for a basic account and eligible deposits are FSCS-protected up to **£120,000 per person**.

| | **Monzo** | **Nationwide FlexAccount** |
|---|---|---|
| **Everyday banking** | App-first: spending notifications, budgeting and account controls are central to the experience. | App and online banking, plus access to **600+ branches**. |
| **Cash and cheques** | Cash deposits at PayPoint or Post Office cost **£1 each**; cheques can be paid in through the app. | Better if you want branch access for banking in person. Check Nationwide’s current terms for the specific way you plan to pay in cash or cheques. |
| **Travel** | Card payments abroad are free; cash-withdrawal limits and fees depend on your account use and plan. | Overseas card use can incur charges, according to its account information. |
| **Interest and rewards** | The basic account isn’t mainly a high-interest current account; savings options are separate. | FlexAccount is the straightforward everyday option. Nationwide also offers other accounts, including FlexDirect, with interest or cashback subject to conditions. |
| **Overdraft** | Available to eligible customers; the rate offered depends on your circumstances. | FlexAccount’s published rate is **39.9% variable** on balances above the first £50. Avoid treating either overdraft as cheap borrowing. |
| **Support style** | Primarily in-app support; no branch network. | Branches can be a real advantage if you want face-to-face service. |

**My take:** If you’re happy doing everything on your phone and rarely deposit cash, I’d lean **Monzo** as the main account. If branch access is important—or you sometimes need to sort something out face to face—I’d lean **Nationwide**.

One detail worth checking before switching: whether you qualify for a Nationwide account with better interest or cashback, and its pay-in requirements. Offers and rates change, so compare the current terms rather than choosing FlexAccount solely for perks available on a different Nationwide account. You can also keep one as a backup while moving your salary and bills over.
